A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PFF/FUR research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments with four language models, four MCQA datasets, MMLU controls, LLM judgments, and a human study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TruthfulQA results and evaluations of additional comparison methods.

M1.justification: The content-token NPO-KL intervention, FF2-only updates, five unlearning iterations, four retain steps, and faithfulness measures remain unchanged. The expanded Section 4.1 and Appendix A explain procedures already documented in v1 Section 5 and Appendix C; NPO+KL is a renamed notation.

E1.justification: v2 adds TruthfulQA, extending evaluation to truthfulness-focused questions within the existing MCQA setting. The original science, sports, and commonsense benchmarks, MMLU controls, and human-study coverage remain.

E2.justification: Appendix B adds evaluated Paraphrasing results in Table 4 and a CC-SHAP evaluation reporting frequent undefined scores. Add-mistake remains the main comparator. Early Answering and Filler Tokens receive discussion without separately reported experimental results.

E3.justification: The added Paraphrasing and CC-SHAP evaluations introduce new testing procedures. CoT-length summaries change from 230/228-instance dataset summaries in v1 Table 5 to per-model summaries over 250/248 instances in v2 Table 6. The retained experiments' zero-shot prompting, model sizes, unlearning budget, and controls remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends learning-rate sensitivity and efficacy–faithfulness analyses to TruthfulQA and diagnoses CC-SHAP's zero-attribution failures. It removes the filtered human-study analysis reporting correlation 0.27 after excluding steps that increased initial-answer probability; the original study and unfiltered correlation remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use Pearson correlations and associated p-values without adding seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or new uncertainty procedures. Updated coefficients and removal of one filtered analysis change results rather than the statistical reporting approach.

E6.justification: v2 adds TruthfulQA results, including LLaMA-3B FUR 85.7% versus Add-mistake 32.9% in Table 2, plus Paraphrasing and CC-SHAP outcomes. Figure 6's correlation changes from 0.933 to 0.889, and Figures 8–9 also change. Most original benchmark scores merely undergo rounding, although LLaMA-8B's Sports Add-mistake value changes from 29.89 to 30.0 beyond equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit mathematical definitions of the gradient-ascent loss, NPO loss, retain-set KL regularizer, and combined objective in Equations 6–9, previously described verbally. This formalizes the existing method; the faithfulness definitions in Equations 1–5 remain unchanged, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The four listed contributions and central claims about parametric faithfulness, changed reasoning, and weak alignment with human plausibility remain. Although the plausibility finding disappears from the abstract, it remains in the introduction and conclusion. The fifth dataset supplies additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds substantive distinctions between post-hoc reasoning and unfaithfulness, explains why paraphrase stability does not establish faithfulness, and interprets CC-SHAP's failures. Section 4.3 adds a rationale for treating one faithful step as capturing a chain's gist. The explicit limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents prefix/content-word input-output pairs and the meaning of an unlearning iteration, adds TruthfulQA learning-rate information, and identifies the CC-SHAP implementation used. Existing prompt templates, core hyperparameters, hardware, costs, and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and new Appendix A substantially expand coverage of machine unlearning, including gradient-based approaches, direct parameter editing, and NPO's relationship to DPO. Appendix B develops positioning against alternative faithfulness tests, and Zaman and Srivastava (2025) joins Yeo et al. as closely related work.

P1.justification: v2 edits the title, abstract, and several explanatory passages, consolidates unlearning details in Section 4.1, and swaps the reasoning-change and human-study subsections. Two new appendices precede the retained appendix material. These changes refine the narrative while preserving most existing prose and the main section structure.

P2.justification: The opening schematic becomes a worked example, and the contextual-versus-parametric diagram is replaced by a two-stage framework overview. v2 also shortens Figure 3, adds a Paraphrasing table, restructures dataset statistics by model, and expands benchmark tables and multi-panel plots for TruthfulQA. These are substantial changes to the paper's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: TruthfulQA and the additional baseline evaluations provide incremental empirical support, while the expanded unlearning explanation makes the implementation easier to assess. These benefits outweigh limited losses, including removal of the filtered human-study analysis. Numerical consistency remains imperfect: v2 Section 6.2 and Figure 6 report 0.889, while Appendix H still reports 0.933.
